title: Jeremy Corners
author: Isaac Banner
notes: The Caller's Box 20362, permission: full. The author's own note: "Author recommends you not call this dance." And the one that decides how it is encoded: "Square through is done in a diamond formation." A two-pass record, the second pass the same with the twos active; the set progresses at the end of each pass, which is what makes the second pass's own selections the next neighbour along. **The square through's foursome is written out** (M9b, DD31): `"who": "self+partner+N1+N2"`, the written relation list `docs/dance-record.md` now documents, is the transcript's "[with twos, W1, and N2 M1]" - four dancers named one at a time and out of two minor sets, which no tag, station list or single relation could say. Both passes write it, so the second pass's `[with N2]` is the same four one progression along. **Measured before and after, and it changes none of the gated oracles**: closure passes at 2, 4 and 6 couples and fails at **37.7359 px** at 3 and 5 either way, reach passes at every length either way, and collision fails at **0.000 px** at every length either way. The one number it does move is `progressed`, 32.0000 -> 37.7359 px at 2 couples. **Both of M9b's owed things are closed** (M9c), and neither was the square through. (a) The `wait-out -> diamond` seam at beat 192 was **32.0000 px, exactly the width of the set**: the waiting couple's crossing really does swap it across, and `planCycle`'s model never learned - the fill that plans a `wait-out` runs after every call, so a pass boundary handed the next pass a couple it still had on the other line. The outs now write back at a pass boundary as well as at a call that carries the progression, and **closure passes at 0.0000 px at every checked length**, where 3 and 5 couples failed at 37.7359. At two and four couples nobody ever waits, which is the whole of why only the odd lengths showed it. (b) B2's single-file promenade is written for three of the four (`who: ["1L","2L","2R"]`) and was planned on a ring of **four**: `{ number: "dancers" }` answered 4, a third of the ring snapped to a quarter turn, and `2L` finished on the place `1R` had been standing on since beat 32. A figure is now planned over the dancers it has (`resolve.ts`'s `castGroup`), the ring is a ring of three with a 120 degree step, and **the beat-56 collision is gone at every length**. **Still owed, one thing, measured: collision 0.000 px at beat 48**, `c0/lark ~ c1/robin` - B1's balance and swing is a gatherer and settles the ones on to the nearest two home places, (16, 20) and (-16, 20), while the twos are still standing on them: `c1/robin` has not moved from (16, 20) since beat 32 and `c1/lark` is stranded at (-6.011, 26.288), because A1's diamond and A2's contra corners leave the inactive couple off its station. At six couples the worst is instead at beat 128, `c4/lark ~ c5/robin`. **Two readings still unsettled by measurement.** (1) The second token of "Square through 2 (NR;SRNL)" could not be read. The first is a neighbour by the right; the second is written here as the partner by the left, because a square through's second hand is with somebody other than the first and a partner is who that is in a diamond. (2) "Ones turn contra corners (along the set)" is `axis: "along"`, which swaps which corner is first. `axis: "across"` was measured too and closes at 32.0000 px at 2, 4 and 6 couples against 37.7359 at 3 and 5, so the transcript's own word is kept and the other reading is a pixel or two better at half the line lengths. Neither changes the motion: `turn-contra-corners` runs a hand at **297.4 px/beat** against a bound of 68.4 either way, because after the diamond the actives are standing in the middle of the set and their corners are a whole dancing place and a half away.

A2  (16) Ones turn contra corners (along the set)
B1  (4) Ones balance  (12) Ones swing; face down
B2  (4) Balance ring  (4) [Man one and twos] Single file promenade clockwise 1/3  (8) Neighbor swing
2A1-2B2: the same with the twos active, [with N2]/[N3] selections.
Author recommends you _not_ call this dance. Square through is done in a diamond formation.
